candidates.demonstrated_gap: The installed writing-for-agents gives writing guidance but no review procedure for the three gaps this task names. This skill covers each of them in CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md: history 'where only the current rule matters' (dated chronology), 'the same rule stated in several places' (single source of truth), and size well past ~1,500 tokens, with reference material moved to linked files (context load). It also checks broken path and command references, README duplication and dated model IDs. Fixes run only with --fix, apply only HIGH-certainty changes, and 'Never delete a rule in a fix'. Its deterministic analyzer (lib/enhance/projectmemory-analyzer.js: validateFileReferences, validateCommandReferences, calculateTokenMetrics at chars/4, detectReadmeDuplication, applyFixes; Node built-ins only) is reached through ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, which Claude Code substitutes only in plugin skills. As a standalone skill or in Codex it is therefore guidance-only. Its command check knows only npm scripts, while this repository's commands are python3 scripts, and it defers to a sibling enhance-prompts skill. On Claude it overlaps the native /doctor prompt-audit (v2.1.283+), which must be a control arm. Source: created 2026-02-21; last default-branch commit 2026-09-27; path rewritten 2026-09-23 (c5601bfd, v1.1.0); 4 stars; no release; no detected license (information only).

Arms run in the same turn per eval. A = writing-for-agents at the installed pin. B = A plus the native /doctor prompt-audit (Claude only; the bundled /claude-api skill must be on). C = A plus enhance-claude-memory, installed as a Claude Code plugin from agent-sh/enhance at c2c669eee61f0530c110459a87e59ed10f762d8d (a pinned marketplace ref, so the analyzer runs) and guidance-only on Codex. Assertions are graded into grading.json and script-checked where possible: every canonical rule from a frozen checklist kept, no rule stated twice, zero broken references, seeded chronology removed, and net bytes not above A. aggregate_benchmark reports pass_rate, tokens and time as mean ± stddev over at least 3 runs per eval. Decision rule (the layer's overturn_when): adopt C only if its pass rate beats both A and B by more than the pooled stddev, at no higher token or time cost, in Claude Code and in Codex. Use keep_but_compare if it wins only on Codex, and not_adopted if it does not beat B on Claude.

candidates.demonstrated_gap:
Serves only the plan branch of the requirement. It reviews an existing requirements, plan or spec document on disk. The coherence and feasibility reviewers always run, plus conditional product, security and adversarial lenses (SKILL.md L41-53). It returns 'consequential choices or essential information only the user can supply' (L11), and 'An adequate document needs no changes' (L9).

In its favour:
- It adds no step to bounded work, because it needs a document.
- It has a real worker contract: mode:non-interactive returns structured findings with no blocking questions (references/modes.md).
- Reviewers run 'inline or serially' where no subagent primitive exists (dispatch.md L3).

Why it is not targeted now:
(1) It cannot run on this layer's frozen request prompts. With no document, non-interactive mode returns 'Review failed: document(s) not found on disk' (document-intake.md L10).
(2) It sends the document to another model family by default. cross_model_review_mode defaults to auto (cross-model-review.md L40). The adversarial lens activates on any 'explicit alternatives section or unresolved tradeoffs' (persona-selection.md L25). The skill then sends the document by direct CLI to the first attested-different family, in the order codex, claude, grok, composer (L47). CROSS_MODEL_PEERS is 'an optional egress restriction, not a required approval' (L49), and non-interactive mode leaves only a stderr audit line (L82). A worker would thus open a cross-family lane, which this repository reserves to the coordinator through OmniRoute. This repository has no .compound-engineering/ config, so auto applies; only cross_model_review_mode: off in that config disables it.
(3) It is heavy: 7.8 KB SKILL.md, about 222 KB of references excluding personas/, and about 200 KB of scripts.
(4) Apply-class fixes edit the reviewed document.

candidates.demonstrated_gap: Codex-native whole-repository audit whose output contract is close to security-audit's. It writes canonical scan-manifest.json, findings.json and coverage.json (SKILL.md L26-27). coverage records reviewed surfaces, exclusions, deferred work and unresolved questions, and is marked complete only when the scope was reviewed (references/core-scan.md L14). Control-based rejections are kept with source anchors in coverage.surfaces[].notes (references/threat-model.md L53). Finalization exports SARIF 2.1.0 (finalize_scan_contract.py L30, L74). Credential question (static reading, not executed): the prompt-only path needs no new credential. finalize_scan_contract.py imports only the standard library (L4-25), and no subprocess, socket or HTTP client was found in it. The .mcp.json env_vars list is a forwarding allowlist (CODEX_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, FIREWORKS_API_KEY, AWS variables), not a set of requirements. Three facts keep this skill at keep_but_compare rather than targeted. (1) The prompt-only path applies only when the host does not offer start_codex_security_standard_scan (SKILL.md L14). Installing the plugin as shipped registers its MCP server (.mcp.json L3-5), so the host-backed path is the default, and that server is a bundled mcp/server.mjs plus brotli parts that cannot be reviewed as source. (2) Without Daybreak access (an account program), 'protected scan outputs may not be displayable' (config-preflight.md L89). (3) In a non-interactive session, the capability preflight applies helper patches to the Codex user config automatically (config-preflight.md L79). A trial therefore needs a disposable CODEX_HOME with a fresh native sign-in, never copied auth files. It is Codex-only, so it cannot meet the both-clients decision rule.

Both scanners tried there were deferred, and the manifest's excluded rows give two reasons. First, superagent-ai/skills@skill-security and getsentry/skills@skill-scanner read through a symlink that resolves outside the target and print a line of the linked file (fixture m7, open() trace), which fails the credential rule. That line sits on top of a deterministic SkillSpector scan (L40, --no-llm, so no model key) and gives APPROVE/CAUTION/REJECT verdicts (L86-90). It forbids silent installs and executing the target's scripts (L24-25). Unknown and gating: the SkillSpector README never mentions symlinks, so its m7 behaviour is unverified. The skill's manual-review commands (find, rg, sed; L26) could also read through an outside link unless an enforced wrapper rejects it. P9's m7 test must therefore pass before any untrusted input. The installed supply-chain-risk-auditor does not cover this gap: its 'When not to use' (L112) says it never reads the target's own source. (2) The documented command fails at the same pin: SKILL.md L49 lists 'plugin-eval benchmark <skill-path> --dry-run', and benchmark.js L497-498 throws 'CLI-only benchmarking no longer supports --dry-run'. The umbrella plugin-eval SKILL.md L61 has the same mismatch. (3) It resolves skills only from ~/.codex/skills or repo-local skills/ (L13), not ~/.agents/skills, where this stack installs shared Codex skills. (4) Its static checks (frontmatter, name/description, links, size; L23-30) overlap Codex's own .system/skill-creator at rust-v0.160.0, which ships scripts/quick_validate.py and an independent forward-testing pass. The package is 'private': true at 0.1.0 (README L24), and the repo has no release and no LICENSE (license is information only). Its sibling improve-skill hard-codes <host-path>/... (L14). Its only unique function is a static trigger/invoke token-budget estimate (explain-budget). For this requirement, the measured tokens and time that skill-creator's benchmark.json and promptfoo's cost and latency assertions already record supersede it. Two active lists went unused: https://github.com/VoltAgent/awesome-agent-skills (89 commits in 28 days) and https://github.com/hesreallyhim/awesome-claude-code (100+ in 28 days). Three other lists are stale under the 90-day rule and should stay out: travisvn/awesome-claude-skills, heilcheng/awesome-agent-skills and skillmatic-ai/awesome-agent-skills.

Neither official vendor marketplace is a source for any layer: Codex's plugin directory https://github.com/openai/plugins (536 SKILL.md files and 513 agents/openai.yaml files at 5fd93af4cd0c) and https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official (33 SKILL.md files at d182ca456ca0). The modelcontextprotocol org is not a source either. Meanwhile the deprecated https://github.com/openai/skills is still a source in 5 layers: browser, ci-pr, design-intake, security and skill-lifecycle.

Some winners stand on incumbency. gh-fix-ci (kept), gh-address-comments (trial), security-best-practices (kept) and security-threat-model (trial) come from openai/skills, which fails the 90-day rule (last default-branch commit 2026-06-24) and calls itself deprecated in its README. openai/plugins offers no successor for the two CI and PR skills. mcp-builder (trial) teaches the MCP SDK 1.x API, while python-sdk and typescript-sdk are on 2.3.0 (2026-10-02).

TOO NEW TO ASSESS (<90 days): typesafe-ai/skills, the source of the review layer's kept winner typesafe-ai, was created 2026-08-24 (https://github.com/typesafe-ai/skills). The layer input cites a verdict row, not a measured comparison.

Discovery was mostly single-family. gpt6 discovery failed in 10 of 13 layers (9 with exit null; security with exit 124, a timeout), so those layers rest on Claude-only discovery. Rerun the cross-family lane before treating them as saturated.

The source pins are current. The compare API from each pin to head shows no SKILL.md added since the pins in mattpocock/skills, affaan-m/ECC, addyosmani/agent-skills, microsoft/skills, vercel-labs/agent-browser, huggingface/skills and anthropics/claude-code. The misses come from the source set, not from stale pins.

Discovery left out methodology packs that ship model-invocable skills across many lifecycle tasks. https://github.com/EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin (MIT, v3.30.3 2026-10-01) was searched only for design-intake. https://github.com/bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD v6 put its skills/ layout in 2026-09-05 and needs the _bmad/ scaffolding. https://github.com/garrytan/gstack (35 commits in 28 days) has very large SKILL.md files. https://github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec (v1.14.0) also ships skills. Judge them per layer under the single-winner rule, not as bundles.

Several evaluation and registry tools need credentials (information only). The promptfoo Claude Agent SDK skill-comparison example uses ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. The NVIDIA SkillEvaluator quickstart uses an NVIDIA API key. tesslio/skill-review needs a Tessl API token (README). Check each against the native sign-in and no-new-credentials rules before adoption.

Layers left out of the top 8 still have leads. Research is the ninth candidate: no proposal survived refutation and gpt6 failed. Its leads are https://github.com/bytedance/deer-flow/tree/fff9d185c522/skills/public/github-deep-research (path last committed 2026-03-27; DeerFlow is already embedded through native-stack-research), assafelovic/gpt-researcher skills/gpt-researcher (12 lines, 2026-04-05) and BMAD skills/bmad-deep-recon (2026-09-29; needs _bmad). For implement, openai/plugins build-web-data-visualization has 18 skills, including dashboards-and-real-time-visualization and testing-data-visualizations, that fit the hand-styled dashboards; only frontend-app-builder from that repository was proposed.

More leads outside the top 8. Architecture: gstack plan-eng-review (2026-10-04; 690 lines) and BMAD bmad-architecture. Review: Codex's built-in system skill review-agent (openai/codex@7f892275e310 codex-rs/skills/src/assets/samples/review-agent, added 2026-07-14 in #33156) was not compared, and neither was compound-engineering ce-code-review (2026-10-01). trailofbits review-walkthrough (added 2026-09-14) is user-invoked only (disable-model-invocation: true; allow_implicit_invocation: false). Browser needs no follow-up: the installed skill ships with the pinned CLI, and compound-engineering ce-test-browser already uses agent-browser as its fallback driver.

Unverified items. Registry facts come from a WebSearch summary and are leads only: SkillsMP (skillsmp.com), the Tessl Registry with Snyk scores (https://snyk.io/blog/snyk-tessl-partnership/) and majiayu000/claude-skill-registry. The arXiv 2608.20614 citation is taken from the SkillEvaluator README, not opened. No candidate code was run, so the runtime credential needs of codex-security and the Workflow-tool dependency of claude-security remain unexecuted claims.

landscape-sweep-skills-20261005-ns2604: Discovery per layer: a Claude researcher (claude-opus-5-5, effort max) and a GPT-6 researcher (gpt-6-astra through the Codex CLI, effort max, web search, read-only sandbox, user config ignored), each proposing at most 6 skills (owner/repo@name) within 12 web searches, 8 page fetches and 40 GitHub API calls; the two returns are merged by skill_ref and capped at 8 per layer (two-family proposals first; dropped proposals are logged and kept under raw).

Adversarial verification per layer: a facts/identity refuter (claude-opus-5-5, effort max) and two fit/standing refuters (claude-opus-5-5 and gpt-6-astra, effort max), each defaulting to refuted, within 8 web searches, 10 page fetches and 30 GitHub API calls; a candidate survives only when no refuter refutes it, and a missing vote counts as refuted.
One completeness critic (claude-opus-5-5, effort max) and one bounded follow-up round over at most 8 critic-flagged layers, with the same roles.

SKILL.md source review and GitHub metadata only: no skill was installed, invoked, benchmarked (skill-creator or promptfoo) or compared with an installed skill; survival means the proposal withstood fact and fit checks, not that it beats an installed skill.

counts.trading_layers_note: trading_layers counts only taxonomy layers with at least one selected entry, unlike foundation_layers (which counts every row); trading[] itself always has one row per taxonomy id, so len(manifest["trading"]) can exceed trading_layers whenever a taxonomy layer happens to have zero selected entries
counts.pin_status_note: pins_behind_upstream counts the generator's computed pin fields; pins_behind_upstream_by_review_status splits those rows by published review_status. A row's review_status is pin_behind_upstream[_unverified] only when its computed pin_behind_upstream is true, so review_status_pin_behind_upstream equals the pin_behind_upstream[_unverified] share of that split; a lane pin claim the computed fields contradict is published as pin_status_disputed[_unverified] (the lane's claim in disputed_lane_status and the row evidence) or, on an OS-package pin, distro_managed
counts.pins_behind_note: components with a commit-pinned version (a parenthetical hash), a non-GitHub repository, or an OS-distribution package pin (matched by an -Nubuntu/-Ndeb/+debN pin suffix, or by id via --os-package-ids, e.g. systemd even though its own repository is on GitHub) are excluded from the pin-vs-upstream comparison rather than counted either way
counts.pins_not_compared_note: rows whose pin the generator could not compare with upstream (the exclusions above, plus a pin or upstream latest with no parseable version, reason unversioned) carry pin_behind_upstream null and pin_comparison not_compared, never a definite false
counts.lane_groupings_note: every foundation/trading-scoped count above (candidates_total, candidates_by_disposition, components_confirmed, pins_behind_upstream, pins_behind_upstream_unique_components) is computed from all_rows = manifest['foundation'] + manifest['trading'] only, and so excludes lane_groupings[].selected rows the same way it excludes lane_groupings[].candidates; candidates inside lane_groupings (a review-lane grouping id outside the foundation/taxonomy baseline, e.g. an awesome-list survey) are counted only in lane_grouping_candidates; counts.citation_review (computed below, by apply_citation_review) is the same way scoped -- its rows_flagged/attached only ever count a foundation/trading row, never a lane_groupings[].selected row, since apply_citation_review only walks manifest['foundation'] and manifest['trading']
